questions.q: In the Schematic Design Phase of Regular Design Services (Doc 202), what is the primary output the architect provides to illustrate the project's concept?
o: Detailed Technical Specifications
Schematic Design Studies (site plans, floor plans, and initial elevations)
Final Structural Calculations
As-Built Drawings
questions.n: This phase focuses on conceptualizing the project's scale and character through visual studies and preliminary plans.

questions.q: During the Design Development Phase, what level of detail is added to the initial schematic drawings?
o: The shop drawings provided by the contractor
Bidding instructions and general conditions
Only bubble diagrams and mood boards
Finalized spatial relationships, structural/MEP layouts, and initial material specifications
questions.n: Design Development 'fixes' the project's size and character by coordinating technical systems and material choices.

questions.q: What is the specific purpose of the Contract Document Phase in the Regular Design Services workflow?
o: To prepare Construction Drawings and Technical Specifications for bidding and permits
To market the project to potential tenants
To conduct initial site selection
To interview prospective workers
questions.n: This phase produces the legally binding technical documents used to obtain permits and select a builder.

questions.q: In the Bidding or Negotiation Phase, what is the architect's duty regarding the selection of the contractor?
o: To pick the contractor with the lowest price automatically
To take legal liability for the contractor's debts
To assist the owner in evaluating bids, analyzing proposals, and preparing the contract
To personally pay the winning bidder's mobilization fee
questions.n: The architect acts as an advisor to ensure the owner chooses a qualified contractor at a fair price.

questions.q: During the Construction Phase, what is the nature of the architect's 'Supervision' under SPP Doc 202?
o: Directing the workers on how to use their tools
Full-time physical presence on the site from start to finish
Periodic Site Visits to check for general compliance and issue Certificates of Payment
Buying materials for the workers on the owner's behalf
questions.n: Standard service requires only regular check-ins, not a full-time site presence.

questions.q: Which service under SPP Doc 203 involves the design of 'Hardscape' (walls, paths) and 'Softscape' (trees, shrubs)?
o: Physical Planning
Interior Design
Landscape Architectural Design Services
Urban Design
questions.n: This service focuses on the outdoor environment and the integration of natural elements.

questions.q: Which Specialized Architectural Service involves the design of the Interior Space, including furniture layout and lighting?
o: Architectural Interiors (AI)
Heritage Conservation
Acoustic Design
Space Management
questions.n: AI covers the detailed design of everything inside the building to enhance function and aesthetic.

questions.q: What is the term for the specialized service that involves the design and layout of Large Land Areas like industrial estates?
o: Building Audit
Architectural Programming
Site Analysis
Physical Planning
questions.n: Physical planning deals with the spatial arrangement of infrastructure and land over large tracts.

questions.q: Which specialized service involves the design of a building’s Acoustics or Specialized Lighting?
o: Building Environment Certification
Acoustic Design or Architectural Lighting Layout and Design
HVAC Design
Structural Engineering
questions.n: These focus on the technical performance of sound and light in specialized environments.

questions.q: What is 'Heritage Conservation' in the context of specialized architectural services?
o: Building a new replica of an old house
Interior design using old-fashioned furniture
The preservation, restoration, or reconstruction of historic structures
Demolishing old buildings to make way for parks
questions.n: This service aims to maintain the historical and cultural significance of existing structures.

questions.q: What is the primary objective of Full-Time Supervision (Doc 204-A)?
o: To calculate the contractor's monthly taxes
To provide marketing photos for the building
To act as the owner's legal lawyer
To ensure work is executed in strict accordance with plans, specs, and quality standards
questions.n: Daily presence allows the supervisor to catch errors immediately before they are covered up.

questions.q: Who is the person physically deployed to the site by the architect to perform the full-time role under Doc 204-A?
o: The Lead Draftsman
The Construction Inspector (or Resident Architect/Engineer)
The Purchasing Officer
The Building Official from City Hall
questions.n: This professional stays on-site to inspect daily progress and quality.

questions.q: Does the Full-Time Supervisor have the authority to stop work if it is non-compliant?
o: No, only the owner can stop work
Yes, they have absolute power over all aspects of the site
Only if the contractor is being rude
Yes, if authorized by the Architect-of-Record (AOR) or the Owner
questions.n: Supervisors must have specific authorization to halt work for non-compliance.

questions.q: What is the supervisor’s duty regarding the construction 'Logbook'?
o: To record the architect's expenses
To keep it at home for privacy
To only write in it when the architect visits
To maintain a daily record of activities, weather, materials, and problems
questions.n: The logbook is the official historical record of the construction site.

questions.q: How is the compensation for Full-Time Supervision usually handled?
o: It is already included in the standard 10% architectural fee
It is paid by the contractor to the architect
It is free if the project is under budget
It is a separate fee, usually a Salary Basis or 1% to 1.5% of construction cost
questions.n: Since it requires a dedicated person on-site, it is billed separately from the main design fee.

questions.q: What is the primary responsibility of a Construction Manager (CM) under Doc 204-B?
o: To physically build the building with their own hands
To provide the funding for the project
To coordinate contractors and ensure project is on time, on budget, and quality-assured
To design the structural beams
questions.n: The CM manages the 'Triple Constraint' of construction for the benefit of the owner.

questions.q: Does a CM assume Civil Liability for the structural integrity of the building under Article 1723?
o: Only if they have a license in engineering
Yes, as the leader of the site
Only if the owner fires the architect
No, the liability remains with the Architect and Engineers of Record
questions.n: The CM has managerial liability, but structural liability always stays with the designers of record.

questions.q: What management tool is typically used by the CM to track the project's schedule?
o: The logbook alone
A standard office calendar
PERT-CPM (Critical Path Method) or Bar Charts
The architect's sketchbook
questions.n: These analytical tools help the CM identify which tasks are critical to meeting the deadline.

questions.q: What is 'Value Engineering' in the context of construction management?
o: Reducing the size of the building to save money
Choosing the most expensive materials to show high value
Reviewing design to find cost-effective alternatives that maintain function and quality
Paying the workers less to increase profit
questions.n: It aims to save money without compromising the building's performance or standard.

questions.q: To whom is the Construction Manager (CM) directly responsible?
o: The Owner
The Architect
The Contractor
The Neighborhood Association
questions.n: The CM is hired by the owner to act as their representative in managing the site.

questions.q: Under SPP Doc 205, what are the two main sub-services included in Post-Construction Services?
o: Renovation and Demolition
Building and Facilities Administration and Post-Occupancy Evaluation (POE)
Painting and Gardening
Security and Janitorial
questions.n: These cover the operation of the building and the assessment of its performance.

questions.q: What is the primary goal of Building and Facilities Administration?
o: To audit the architect's original drawings
To manage daily operations, maintenance, and security to preserve building value
To design the building's anniversary party
To sell the building for a profit
questions.n: It ensures the building remains functional and profitable over its entire life.

questions.q: What is a Post-Occupancy Evaluation (POE)?
o: A systematic study performed after the building is occupied to see if it meets user needs
Checking if the building was built according to the permit
A party held for the tenants
Evaluating the building's value for tax purposes
questions.n: POE gathers data from users to see if the design actually works in practice.

questions.q: In building administration, what is 'Preventive Maintenance'?
o: Scheduling regular inspections and repairs to prevent major failures
Hiring a security guard
Fixing an elevator only after it stops working
Closing the building to prevent people from breaking things
questions.n: Proactive care extends the life of building systems and prevents decay.

questions.q: How is the architect usually compensated for these long-term management services under Doc 205?
o: By charging the contractors a commission
Through gifts from the tenants
Usually through a Fixed Salary or a Percentage of Gross Monthly Income
With a one-time lump sum at the end of construction
questions.n: Since management is an ongoing task, the architect is paid like an executive or on a share of revenue.
